rationale: Author-of-record walk of plan §Bead 9 (plan.md:1143-1162) against git show 2691189d: all three steps delivered faithfully, at the layers the plan names, and only them. Step 1: wrapBDError is applied inside tracedOutput (internal/bead/bdcli.go:523-527), the single cmd.Output() choke point, so RunBD, ListJSON ('list'), GetMetadata/FetchBead ('show'), and 'worktree-list' ALL benefit — verified by grepping tracedOutput's callers. tracedCombined is correctly left untouched: CombinedOutput merges stderr into the returned output, leaving exec.ExitError.Stderr empty, so there is nothing to fold there. The cap is pinned in bdcli.go exactly as the plan requires ('cap pinned here'): bdStderrExcerptLineCap = 20, with a rationale comment tying it to the #146 schema-error class, and the truncation marker names the cap value. 20 is sane — real bd/Dolt diagnostics are 1-5 lines; the cap only bounds pathological emitters. Step 2: only the two planned wrap sites (QueryReady, QueryReadyForEpic) changed in internal/next/beads.go; renderBDError escapes per line via termsafe.Escape, which returns all-printable-ASCII lines byte-identical (internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:37-44) — legitimate diagnostics are not rewritten, matching the DirtyTreeFailure house pattern the plan cites. No unrelated-caller message rewrites anywhere: FetchBeadByID/FetchBeadAsOf and every other beads.go message are untouched, and the commit's four files (bdcli.go, bdcli_test.go, beads.go, beads_test.go) do not intersect parallel bead 7's surface (internal/next/guard.go, cmd/mindspec/next.go). Step 3: both AC-11 legs are asserted separately, and the rendering-leg test is constructed so a raw-passthrough regression (bare %w) would pass the content leg but fail the rendering leg — exactly the asymmetry AC-11 names. Chain integrity: wrapBDError wraps with %w, and the two errors.As consumers (BeadExists at bdcli.go:96-99, IsUnsupportedFlagError at bdcli.go:115-122) are regression-pinned through the real tracedOutput chain (TestRunBD_EmptyStderrUnchanged, TestIsUnsupportedFlagError_SurvivesTracedOutputWrapping). Verified firsthand in the bead worktree at 2691189d (clean, byte-identical): go build ./... green; go test -short -count=1 on internal/bead (ok 5.8s) and internal/next (ok 10.1s) green. A whole-tree go test ./... -short run was still executing at verdict-write time with no failures observed; the implementer reports 48/48 and every bead's AC-13 verification re-runs it.

findings.title: QueryReady/QueryReadyForEpic wrap with %s (renderBDError) instead of %w — error chain intentionally cut at the render boundary; verified no consumer depended on it
findings.detail: beads.go:39 and beads.go:55 switch from %w to %s so the escaped text (not the raw underlying error) is what propagates. This is a necessary consequence of the plan's directive to escape inside the wrapping-message construction, but it does drop errors.As/Is reachability of the underlying *exec.ExitError from these two functions' returns. I verified every caller: cmd/mindspec/next.go:180 and :443 only fmt.Errorf('querying ready work: %w', err) for terminal rendering — no errors.As/Is anywhere on the QueryReady/QueryReadyForEpic error path. No change required; noting so a future caller wanting programmatic detection knows to probe at the internal/bead layer instead.

findings.title: Whole-tree -short verification was in flight at verdict time
findings.detail: Build plus the two touched packages' suites were verified green firsthand in the bead worktree. The full-tree go test ./... -short -count=1 (the plan's verification checkbox) had produced no failures but had not completed when the panel deadline required this verdict; the BRIEF reports it green (48/48) and AC-13's method gate re-runs it at bead 10 and in CI. If the tally wants a firsthand full-tree confirmation from this slot, treat this finding as the pointer.
